simple.meaning: אֲרָמִית (ʼĂrâmîyth) is a Hebrew word meaning “(only adverbial) in Aramæan.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אֲרָמִית (H762) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Kings 18:26, with occurrences in 2 Kings, Ezra, Isaiah, Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲרָמִית (H762) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אֲרָמִית (H762) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אֲרָמִית (ʼĂrâmîyth) / H762 is traced through 2 Kings 18:26, Ezra 4:7, Isaiah 36:11, Daniel 2:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, Shebnah, and Joah, said to Rabshakeh, “Please speak to your servants in the Syrian language, for we understand it. Don’t speak with us in the Jews’ language, in the hearing of the people who are on the wall.”

timeline.evidenceText: Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, Shebnah, and Joah, said to Rabshakeh, “Please speak to your servants in the Syrian language, for we understand it. Don’t speak with us in the Jews’ language, in the hearing of the people who are on the wall.”

In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his companions, wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia; and the writing of the letter was written in Syrian, and delivered in the Syrian language.

In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his companions, wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia; and the writing of the letter was written in Syrian, and delivered in the Syrian language.

Then Eliakim, Shebna and Joah said to Rabshakeh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Don’t speak to us in the Jews’ language in the hearing of the people who are on the wall.”
Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in the Syrian language, “O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will show the interpretation.”
